summary.text: A 55-year-old man with no previous medical history spent about a month and a half in Guinea and, by his own report, took doxycycline 100 mg/day as prophylaxis. On day 4 after returning home he developed cough and high fever, and on day 5 he was diagnosed with pneumonia, considered atypical, doxycycline was stopped and azithromycin started. He was hospitalized on day 8 with fever, extreme fatigue and sudden loss of consciousness.

On admission he was alert with a Glasgow coma scale of 15, febrile at 39 °C, with oxygen saturation 92% on room air, moderate dehydration, moderate scleral jaundice and slightly enlarged liver and spleen; admission platelets were 86 × 10^(9)/L. Reported laboratory values also showed elevated bilirubin, urea 19.45 mmol/L and creatinine 223.7 µmol/L. Chest X-ray showed right lung opacities and ultrasound showed hepato-splenomegaly and increased kidney size. A positive malaria test and a thin smear showing Plasmodium falciparum with 20% parasitemia confirmed severe falciparum malaria, complicated by acute kidney injury.

Because parenteral antimalarials were unavailable, he received oral artemether-lumefantrine for 6 days from hospital day 1, with IV ceftriaxone, rehydration, supportive therapy and transfusions. For serious renal deterioration he had five dialysis cycles from day 3. He was febrile for the first three days, blood tests worsened during the first week and improved in the second, and urine production improved from day 8.

After 14 days of intensive care he was discharged in improved condition with urine production normalized and creatinine 112 µmol/L. A thin smear on the last hospital day showed no signs of parasitemia. Examination and blood tests two weeks after hospitalization showed complete clinical and laboratory recovery.
